drivers.variant_notes: Code update V23 (AMH_SD_V023.zip from benheck.com with AMH_V023.hex added to the root, as the PinMAME pull request describes; the PIC32 runs the Intel HEX, the Propeller PROP_023.BIN (CRC bd5a99e8) from DMD/), loaded as amh_023.zip. Every edition (IPDB 6161 America's Most Haunted) runs this code on the same board and playfield; PinMAME declares the set as a clone of the unreported pinHeck system set. PinMAME revisions before 97aa922b named it `amh`.

The earlier code update V22 (the card's VERSION.TXT: code and A/V revision 22, dated 10/3/2015): benheck.com's AMH_SD.zip card with AMH_V022.hex from its pinball_update_hex folder added to the root; the PIC32 runs the Intel HEX (CRC b74f2a7b), the Propeller DMD/PROP_022.bin (CRC 53a6b98b). It runs on the same board and playfield and shares V23's switch, lamp and output definitions in PinMAME. Every retained runtime run used V23; PinMAME notes that its DMD frame address is verified for V23 only, while the display itself is decoded from the scan pins. Sources rom.amh-v22-card and rom.amh-v22-hex record both downloads, the card's VERSION.TXT and the CRC check. PinMAME loads it as amh_022.zip.

physical.notes: Firmware cabinet input 1 (U12 D0), published at 1 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk toggled it separately (released, then held again) instead of closing it. The factory chart prints 'COIN DOOR OPEN' in this cell. pinheck_brd_reset sets it at every reset because the door rests closed; the ROM printed DOOR CLOSE while it was 1 and dropped the text when the host released it, so 1 means the door is closed. The chart cell adds '(gray)'.

Firmware cabinet input 2 (U12 D1), published at 2 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure as firmware cabinet 2. PinMAME's port names the bit User; the factory chart leaves it blank and the cabinet header prints 'user0' without a wire colour.

Firmware cabinet input 3 (U12 D2), published at 3 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk drives the button through 112 instead, because core_updateSw rewrites this address every vblank. ROM-readable copy of the right flipper button: FLIP_SWNO(4, 3) makes core_updateSw copy public 112 into this address on every vblank, so a host drives 112; a direct write here is overwritten. The chart cell adds '(Purp / black)'.

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball lands on the drain switch 88 and the DRAIN KICK coil (22) kicks it into the four-ball trough, sensed by 84-87 (Trough Ball 1-4). BALL LOAD (21) feeds one ball to the shooter lane (82). In the game-start run (all four trough contacts closed, Start pressed) the ROM pulsed 21 about every 1.6 s for 20 s, because no ball ever reached 82 to close it.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough, drain kicker and ball loader

mechanisms.behavior: AUTOPLUNGER (23) kicks the ball resting on the shooter lane switch 82 into play; PinMAME's simulator also offers a manual plunger here.
mechanisms.label: Shooter lane and autolauncher

mechanisms.behavior: A ROM-driven flipper on two board coils: the cabinet button reaches the ROM as cabinet input 3 (host public 112), the ROM fires the RFLIP HIGH (17) winding to lift the bat and holds it on the RFLIP HOLD (18) winding, and the matrix end-of-stroke contact 75 (RIGHT EOS) tells it the stroke is complete. PinMAME publishes no Fliptronic states for this platform: the coil addresses are the flipper.
mechanisms.label: Right flipper

mechanisms.behavior: A ROM-driven flipper on two board coils: the cabinet button reaches the ROM as cabinet input 4 (host public 114), the ROM fires the LFLIP HIGH (19) winding to lift the bat and holds it on the LFLIP HOLD (20) winding, and the matrix end-of-stroke contact 74 (LEFT EOS) tells it the stroke is complete. PinMAME publishes no Fliptronic states for this platform: the coil addresses are the flipper.
mechanisms.label: Left flipper

mechanisms.behavior: Slingshot switch 73 closes and the ROM fires LSLING (9).
mechanisms.label: Left slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Slingshot switch 76 closes and the ROM fires RSLING (10).
mechanisms.label: Right slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Pop bumper 0: skirt switch 56, coil POP BUMP 0 (14), the wire chart's upper left pop.
mechanisms.label: Pop bumper 0 (upper left)

mechanisms.behavior: Pop bumper 1: skirt switch 67, coil POP BUMP 1 (15), the wire chart's upper right pop.
mechanisms.label: Pop bumper 1 (upper right)

mechanisms.behavior: Pop bumper 2: skirt switch 66, coil POP BUMP 2 (16), the wire chart's lower pop.
mechanisms.label: Pop bumper 2 (lower)

mechanisms.behavior: The basement: lanes 54 (Basement Upper) and 55 (Basement Lower) lead to the basement right scoop (37), which SCOOPKICK (11) ejects; the IPDB features count two vertical up-kickers.
mechanisms.label: Basement scoop

mechanisms.behavior: The Spooky Door is servo 1 (58): the ROM's Servo test sets DOOR OPEN (level 7) and DOOR CLOSE (level 128). Behind it the VUK (12) lifts a ball resting on 38 (VUK LEFT BEHIND DOOR); opto 96 (the Spooky Door opto on the aux board) sees a ball at the door.
mechanisms.label: Spooky Door and the VUK behind it

mechanisms.behavior: The Hellevator car is servo 0 (57): HELL UP (level 228) and HELL DOWN (level 14) in the Servo test. Switch 64 senses a ball in the car and 46 is the elevator call button target; IPDB describes it carrying the ball to upper and lower levels.
mechanisms.label: Hellevator

mechanisms.behavior: LOOP MAGNET (1) on the ghost loop, with the Ghost Loop opto 95 (opto 1 on the aux board) seeing the ball pass.
mechanisms.label: Ghost loop magnet

mechanisms.behavior: The ghost figure turns on servo 2 (59: GHOST LEFT 14, MIDDLE 128, RIGHT 242 in the Servo test) and glows from on-board WS2801 LED 2. Red is 62; green and blue are 63 and 64 under the RGB test's default GHOST TYPE REV 1 and swap to 64 and 63 under REV 2, an operator setting. IPDB calls it a colour-changing ghost.
mechanisms.label: Ghost figure

mechanisms.behavior: Ghost targets 1-3 (33-35) on a bank that servo 3 (60) raises and lowers: TARGET UP (level 7) and TARGET DOWN (level 228). IPDB: the 3-target bank drops into the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Three-target bank

mechanisms.behavior: The balcony jump: 52 senses the approach, 51 a successful jump and 53 a ball that falls short onto the pop path.
mechanisms.label: Balcony jump ramp
